kanzAlMahalliRecord.statement: In each spouse-plus-parents case, the mother receives one third of the remainder after the spouse, leaving the father twice the mother's amount.

khulasaRecord.locator: references/source-notes/khulasa/khulasa-full.pdf; printed page 270; mother with one spouse and both parents, including footnote 10.
khulasaRecord.statement: The text and footnote give both exact cases: husband with both parents from six, and wife with both parents from four.

supportingSourceStatus: No project-local Fath al-Mu‘in locator was available, so none is asserted.
ruleSummary: In the two Umariyyatayn, the mother takes one third of the post-spouse remainder rather than one third of the whole estate.
conditions: Case one contains exactly husband, mother, and father among the supported heir categories.
Case two contains a wife group, mother, and father among the supported heir categories.
No descendant or other heir changes the named spouse-plus-parents configuration.
exclusions: Do not apply the mother's ordinary one-third-of-the-whole atom in either named case.
Additional heirs take the case outside these atomic Umariyyatayn rules.
The wife's one-quarter is collective if more than one eligible wife is represented by the wife group.
blockingAndPriorityInteractions: Assign the spouse fixed share first.
Assign the mother one third of the exact remainder.
Assign the father the balance, which is twice the mother's amount.

sourceAgreement.detail: Both sources give the same remainder-third treatment and the same exact shares in both cases.

atomicCandidateAssessment.rationale: The spouse share and resulting original case denominator differ, so each Umariyyatayn case is a separate atom.

admissionBlockers: Exact fixtures and a separate calculation-readiness admission remain required.
